artworks.title: "Queen Tomyris With The Head of Cyrus"
artworks.artist: Francesco Fontebasso, Jules Allard et ses Fils (designer)
artworks.description:
"Queen Tomyris With The Head of Cyrus" and oil on canvas ceiling painting by Francesco Salvator Fontebasso (Italian, 1707-1769) installed above the main staircase of The Elms. The foreground depicts an enthroned Queen Tomyris surrounded by courtiers beneath a red and gold canopy raised on a white marble staircase. Below, stands a warrior before his soldiers presenting her with the head of Cyrus the Great, King of Persia. The background features classical architecture and a balcony filled with onlookers. The sides (19th century) are grisaille decorated with male nudes, mascarons, and scrolling foliage. Queen Tomyris was the ruler of the Massagetae, who were responsible for the execution by decapitation of Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, and Master of Western Asia. The scene was the subject of a celebrated painting by Peter Paul Rubens. The decapitated head of Cyrus was overpainted by the studios of Jules Allard et ses fils ca. 1898 for installation in The Elms to render the scene less horrific.

This painting was originally located in the Palazzo Duodo a Sta Maria Zobenigo in Venice. It was removed in 1888 and made its way to The Elms in 1901, where it was placed above the staircase as a ceiling canvas.

artworks.title: Ceiling Painting of "Dawn" or "Dawn Chasing Away the Darkness of Night"
artworks.description: An oil on canvas mythological ceiling painting installed in the Drawing Room of The Elms entitled "Dawn" alternatively known as "Dawn Chasing Away the Darkness of Night" by Jacob de Wit (Dutch, 1695-1754). The lower right corner depicts Boreas and Aquilo being driven from the sky by Dawn with her torch, accompanied by Flora and the zephyrs, the gentle winds. Flora wears a long red dress with white drapery and carries flowing vines overhead while Dawn wears pink with blue drapery. Dawn's court of zephyrs wear variously bright colored clothing. All are set against a cloud-swept light blue sky with multiple putti, the borders of the canvas depict retreating grey clouds.

artworks.title: Wicker Side Chair
artworks.dimensions: H 38.75 inches · W 19.5 inches · D 17.5 inches
artworks.description: A green painted wicker side chair made by the Wakefield Rattan Co., Wakefield, MA. The chair has a fan back with decorative scrolls, a round seat, and is raised on four legs. The front two legs are cabriole while the back two are splayed. The legs are connected by an X-stretcher, the knees of the front legs have decorative scrolls.

artworks.title: Carved Walnut Library Table
artworks.dimensions: H 34 inches · W 84 inches · D 53.25 inches
artworks.description: A Francois I style carved walnut library table from the workshops of Jules Allard & Sons of Paris. The inlaid rectangular top sits above a leaf-carved frieze containing two drawers on the long sides and is raised on trestle-type male and female figural supports that terminate in scroll-shaped feet. The supports connect to a full length medial stretcher/footer composed of C-scrolls centering on a lion's mask on an egg and dart carved base. The sides have Doric pilasters flanking archways with pendant drops.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Library: carved walnut panelling and a Renaissance-style fireplace
artworks.placeNote: A carved walnut library table from the house (our guess: the Society doesn’t say which room it is in today).

artworks.title: Renaissance Revival Oak Dining Table
artworks.description: A Renaissance Revival parcel-gilt and carved oak dining table by Jules Allard & Sons of Paris. The rectangular top features rounded corners above parcel-gilt fluted classical columns repeating in a round arched gallery series and with leonine mask-and-paw carved corner supports over a stretcher base with parcel-gilt foliate reserves. The scrolled feet also have parcel-gilt leaf carving.
artworks.credit: Purchase by The Preservation Society of Newport County, 2007.
artworks.imageCredit: The Preservation Society of Newport County
artworks.galleryName: Dining Room: the Berwinds’ formal dining room, with Venetian paintings
artworks.placeNote: The Berwinds’ dining table, made by Allard, who made the room (our guess: the Society doesn’t say which room it is in today).

artworks.title: L'aurore (Aurora)
artworks.artist: Jean Joseph Vinache (after), Jules Allard et ses Fils (designer)
artworks.dimensions: H 81 inches · W 44 inches · D 41 inches
artworks.description: A white marble sculpture of L’aurore (Aurora) from the studio of Jules Allard et ses Fils depicting a nude, winged goddess riding a cloud, facing left and carrying a flaming torch. In her outstretched hand and strewn around her feet are several roses. She can be found on the upper terrace of The Elms grounds. This work by Allard is a 19th century French copy after the original by Jean-Joseph Vinache, (French, 1696-1754) executed in 1750. In the 19th century her features were falsely said to be modeled after Madame de Pompadour, the mistress of King Louis XV. The original marble statue was on the grounds of the Chateau de Menars, the former Loire Valley chateau of Madame de Pompadour and her brother, the Marquis de Marigny.

artworks.placeNote: On the upper terrace (its record in the Preservation Society’s collection); “Female Figure with Torch” on the Society’s 1992 sketch map of the grounds and its statuary list (National Historic Landmark nomination).

artworks.title: L'abondance (Abundance)
artworks.artist: Lambert-Sigisbert Adam (after), Jules Allard et ses Fils (designer)
artworks.dimensions: H 84 inches · W 36 inches · D 50 inches
artworks.description: A white marble sculpture entitled “L’abondance” (“Abundance”) from the studio of Jules Allard and Sons after a 1758 century sculpture by Lambert-Sigibert Adam (French, 1700-1759), also known as Adam the Elder. Representing the divine personification of prosperity, the nude female sculpture carries an overflowing cornucopia with fruit spilling out around the base. The traits of the original were erroneously said in the nineteenth century to be modeled after Madame de Pompadour, as the original marble was at Chateau de Menars, the former Loire Valley Chateau of Madame de Pompadour and later her brother the Marquis de Marigny.

artworks.title: Louis XVI Style Rolltop Desk
artworks.dimensions: H 53.5 inches · W 65.25 inches · D 31.75 inches
artworks.description: A Louis XVI style gilt-bronze mounted mahogany bureau a cylindre (rolltop desk) by the firm Zwiener-Jansen of Maison Jansen. The cylinder front opens to numerous pigeonholes and a gold-tooled brown leather pull-out writing slide. A single frieze drawer below, flanked by cupboard doors opening to small drawers. Fluted, round tapering legs. Richly mounted in bronze dore with "amor" escutcheons, laurel swags, and two pairs of candle arms. The reverse with a large panel of amors holding a medallion of "Minerva."

artworks.title: A Louis XV Style Kingwood Bureau Plat
artworks.dimensions: H 35.75 inches · W 67 inches · D 36.75 inches
artworks.description: A Louis XV Style kingwood bureau plat possibly by Krieger of Paris. The ornate desk is inspired by the "Medallion Commode", a chest of drawers designed by Sebastien-Antoine Slodtz (1695-1754) and manufactured by the Royal cabinetmaker Antoine Gaudreaux (c.1681-1751) for delivery in 1739 to Louis XV’s private apartments at Versailles. In the King’s chambers the commode served to display medals commemorating important events during the reign of Louis XIV and the youth of Louis XV. At the front and back of the desk is a central mask of a woman, her headdress extends to the sides and garlands of flowers hang off them and trail across the entirety of the piece. The central drawer is flanked by cupboard drawers, decorated with scrolling acanthus leaves, garlands, and hanging medals with portraits of Roman emperors. Both sides feature a central medallion surrounded by garlands, metals, and acanthus leaves. One medallion depicts a woman sitting astride on a large cat, a staff in her right hand. The other depicts the Greek hero Hercules with a club and a lion skin draped over his left arm, an altar with flame to his left. The whole is raised on four large cabriole legs, each with scroll feet and ram heads.
artworks.credit: Purchase by The Preservation Society of Newport County, 2002.

artworks.title: Portrait of Edward J. Berwind, Esq.
artworks.dimensions: H 46 1/4 inches · W 36 1/4 inches · D · [Diam] · L · [Remarks]Framed
artworks.description: An oil on canvas portrait of Edward J. Berwind, Esq. (1848 - 1936) of The Elms by Fred W. Wright. Berwind is depicted seated in a Louis XIII style chair, facing forward, with wavy gray hair and a gray moustache and wearing a black jacket and tie over a white shirt. His tie is accented with a pearl pin, and his hands are resting in lap. Painting is housed in a molded rectangular giltwood frame.
artworks.credit: Gift of Mr. Charles E. Dunlap, 1964.

artworks.placeNote: A portrait of Edward J. Berwind (our guess: the Society doesn’t say which room it is in today).

artworks.title: A Louis XVI Style Dressing Table and Mirror
artworks.dimensions: H 80 inches · W 49 inches · D 26.5 inches
artworks.description: A Louis XVI style dressing table and mirror from Jules Allard & Sons of Paris. The table has a rectangular top above a conforming frieze containing five drawers. Each of the drawers has egg and dart banding with bronze scrolling leaf-shape handles. The table has four fluted legs with acanthus leaves and accented blocks at the feet. Above the table is a large, shaped mirror in an elaborate frame with scroll-shaped sides accented by large florets. Both sides of the frame terminate in pinecone shaped finials. At the center is a floral wreath trophy tied with a stylized bow and ribbon.
